dedupe_keys.name: ambulance deployment and redeployment dataset for the fez meknes region morocco

description: This data set describes the demand for ambulances and the candidate ambulance stations across the Fez-Meknes region of Morocco, prepared so that researchers can build and compare models that decide where ambulances should wait and how to move them as calls come in. The producers are Youness Frichi and Fouad Jawab of Sidi Mohamed Ben Abdellah University and Lina Aboueljinane of the École Nationale Supérieure des Mines de Rabat. Coverage is 199 demand areas grouped by prefecture and province, with three sets of 18, 22 and 40 potential ambulance sites. Sixteen tables give each area's coordinates and population, demand by ambulance type (advanced or basic life support) and time period, call arrival rates, and the travel data needed to link areas and sites. The workbook is available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: demand values are derived from population and assumptions, not observed call records, travel times are modelled, and hospital capacity is not included. Simulation uses: benchmarking ambulance location and redeployment optimisation and discrete-event simulations, and testing how losing stations or roads in a disaster lengthens response times. Related records: the ambulance models JEMSS (model-jemss) and OpenEMS (model-openems-ambulance-deployment) can use such inputs, and the São Paulo ambulance data generator (data-sao-paulo-ambulance-occurrence-generator) offers another test case.
